To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the inertial modes in a rapidly rotating non-stratified neutron star are the same as those found in the Cowling approximation and are not modified by the effects of rotation; (2) the g modes in a rapidly spinning stratified neutron star are rotation dominated and approach the inertial modes as the rotation rate is increased; (3) the inertial and g modes are stable against gravitational radiation reaction in the Cowling and fully relativistic approximation.
the g modes of rotating neutron stars are not inertial modes and that the g modes are not unstable to gravitational radiation.
